sn36.11:1.1: Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn36.11:1.2: “Here, venerable sir, while I was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in my mind thus:
sn36.11:1.3: ‘Three feeling have been spoken of by the Blessed One:
sn36.11:1.4: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
sn36.11:1.5: These three feelings have been spoken of by the Blessed One.
sn36.11:1.6: But the Blessed One has said:
sn36.11:1.7: “Whatever is felt is included in suffering.”
sn36.11:1.8: Now with reference to what was this stated by the Blessed One?’”
sn36.11:2.2: These three feelings have been spoken of by me:
sn36.11:2.3: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
sn36.11:2.4: These three feelings have been spoken of by me.
sn36.11:2.6: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’
sn36.11:2.7: That has been stated by me with reference to the impermanence of formations. That has been stated by me with reference to formations being subject to destruction …
sn36.11:2.9: to formations being subject to vanishing …
sn36.11:2.11: to formations being subject to fading away …
sn36.11:2.12: to formations being subject to cessation …
sn36.11:2.13: to formations being subject to change.
sn36.11:2.15: “Then, bhikkhu, I have also taught the successive cessation of formations.
sn36.11:2.16: For one who has attained the first jhana, speech has ceased.
sn36.11:2.17: For one who has attained the second jhana, thought and examination have ceased.
sn36.11:2.18: For one who has attained the third jhana, rapture has ceased.
sn36.11:2.19: For one who has attained the fourth jhana, in-breathing and out-breathing have ceased.
sn36.11:2.20: For one who has attained the base of the infinity of space, the perception of form has ceased.
sn36.11:2.21: For one who has attained the base of the infinity of consciousness, the perception pertaining to the base of the infinity of space has ceased.
sn36.11:2.22: For one who has attained the base of nothingness, the perception pertaining to the base of the infinity of consciousness has ceased.
sn36.11:2.23: For one who has attained the base of neither-perception-nor-nonperception, the perception pertaining to the base of nothingness has ceased.
sn36.11:2.24: For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased.
sn36.11:2.25: For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, lust has ceased, hatred has ceased, delusion has ceased.
sn36.11:2.26: “Then, bhikkhu, I have also taught the successive subsiding of formations.
sn36.11:2.27: For one who has attained the first jhana speech has subsided….
sn36.11:2.29: For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have subsided.
sn36.11:2.30: For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, lust has subsided, hatred has subsided, delusion has subsided.
sn36.11:2.31: “There are, bhikkhu, these six kinds of tranquillization.
sn36.11:2.32: For one who has attained the first jhana, speech has been tranquillized.
sn36.11:2.33: For one who has attained the second jhana, thought and examination have been tranquillized.
sn36.11:2.34: For one who has attained the third jhana, rapture has been tranquillized.
sn36.11:2.35: For one who has attained the fourth jhana, in-breathing and out-breathing have been tranquillized.
sn36.11:2.36: For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have been tranquillized.
sn36.11:2.37: For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, lust has been tranquillized, hatred has been tranquillized, delusion has been tranquillized.”
